page: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions.

Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation that conforms to standard enterprise memory-intensive design patterns. In memory subsystem benchmarks, the instance achieves 839.97 GB/sec for small-block cached reads and 102.72 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads, alongside 57.37 GB/sec in write throughput. Ephemeral block storage consists of an included 644 GB local solid-state drive (SSD), suitable for swap space, caches, or temporary runtime data, with additional support for Azure Premium Storage attachments.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent of tested cloud servers in its class. It records a Geekbench single-core score of 1577.0 and a multi-core score of 9397.0, along with a PassMark CPU score of 21141.48. In storage and memory processing workloads, the instance delivered 15.88 million Redis SET operations per second and handled 7921.71 database operations per second in PassMark tests. Small-model LLM inference (135M) reached 1009.79 tokens per second in prompt processing, whereas medium (7B) models executed at 34.35 prompt tokens per second and 11.61 generation tokens per second.

Without integrated GPUs, the server is ill-suited for heavy deep learning training or graphics tasks. However, its high memory-to-core ratio and bundled local NVMe-class SSD offer a cost-effective operational balance for in-memory caching tiers, relational database hosting, large-scale ETL pipelines, and enterprise data analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure E16bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for data-heavy enterprise workloads. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from an 8-core Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, supported by 128.0 GB of RAM (8.0 GB per vCPU) and a bundled 644 GB local SSD. Equipped with AVX-512 vector extensions and 48 MB of L3 cache, the system demonstrates solid throughput across benchmarks, achieving 102.72 GB/sec in uncached read memory bandwidth and 15.88 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations. While it lacks discrete hardware acceleration for large AI training, its high memory density and local temporary disk make it well balanced for relational databases, Redis caching layers, analytical ETL jobs, and enterprise application deployments.
